name: Question 5
problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ at the point where $t=\pi ,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
worked_solution:
At the point where $t=\pi ,$ the vector ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as
 

$$
R(u)=r(\pi )+u{r}^{′}(\pi ),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where $t=\pi $ is

$$
R(u)=⟨-1,0⟩+u⟨0,1⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 5
?

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩ at the point where t=π, valid for all real values of u?

a
⟨−1,0⟩+u⟨−1,0⟩
b
⟨1,1⟩+u⟨0,1⟩
c
⟨−1,0⟩+u⟨−1,1⟩
d
⟨−1,0⟩+u⟨0,1⟩
e
⟨1,1⟩+u⟨−1,0⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

At the point where t=π, the vector r′(π) is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at P can be parametrized as R(u)=r(π)+ur′(π),u∈(−∞,∞)

First, we find r(π): r(π)=⟨cos⁡π,−sin⁡π⟩=⟨−1,0⟩

Now, we calculate r′(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(cos⁡t),ddt(−sin⁡t)⟩=⟨−sin⁡t,−cos⁡t⟩

Then, we evaluate r′(t) at t=π: r′(π)=⟨−sin⁡π,−cos⁡π⟩=⟨0,1⟩

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where t=π is
R(u)=⟨−1,0⟩+u⟨0,1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞).
